content.text: DnD 5.5’s
Shifting Combatant

feat, introduced in “D&D Beyond Drops”, encourages players to dive into melee with a big weapon and push their enemies around. Domino Strike provides an extra incentive to use Push weapons and crowd enemies into small spaces, which is always great if you have allies who can do area damage.

Shifting Combatant recieved errata in the August 2026 Drops, changing the effect of Domino Strike to deal 1d10 damage to creatures that fail their save instead of knocking them Prone. The damage doesn’t scale, so it quickly feels obsolete.

Strength or Dexterity. Great for the martial characters like to use this. Fearless Strike will generally restrict this to Strength-based builds because there are so few Dexterity-based Push weapons, but heavy crossbows have Push and you could get Weapon Mastery on a Monk and use a qualifying weapon with Dexterity.

Bad damage with no scaling, it only works with a specific Weapon Mastery, and you can only use it if you have two enemies close enough together to trigger this. Unfortunately, you can’t use this on an enemy already in the second enemy’s space, so it may be difficult to trigger this multiple times in a turn.

Because the creature affected by Push doesn’t explicitly stop when it hits another creature, it appears that you can trigger this against multiple enemies. If you have three enemies in a straight line, you may be able to trigger Domino Strike twice with one attack. The text also doesn’t address
multiple creautres occupying a single space
, so it’s possible that every creature in the space makes the save, but I think the intent is to only affect one creature. Talk to your DM.

There’s no explanation of how this interacts with other forced movement effects, such as the Crusher feat or the Barbarian’s Brutal Strikes feature. I think the closest we can get to rules as intended is that Domino Strike only applies to the 10 feet applied by the Push Weapon Mastery, so you could use other forced movement effects to get your target close to the secondary target(s), then apply the Push effect and trigger Domino Strike. Again, talk to your DM.

A great way to dive into crowds on enemies. If your AC isn’t great, this is a fantastic defense. Barbarians using Reckless Attack can use this to offset the drawback, allowing them to use it at much less risk. The only problem is that it requires two enemies close enough together for you to land adjacent to both of them, which you can’t always guarantee even in fights with multiple enemies, but you’re almost certainly using a Push weapon, so you can creature your own crowd to jump into.
Long Jump allows you to jump a horizontal distance
up to

your Strength score. 0 feet is less than your Strength score, so you can move 10 feet, jump 0 feet, and trigger Fearless Strike. If you’re playing on a grid, distances are rounded down to the nearest 5 feet, so you could jump 4 feet and still not reach the next square. Sometimes you’ll want the movement distance, but travelling exactly 2 squares may let you use this without provoking an Opportunity Attack if you’re already in melee.

Starting in April of 2026, DnD Beyond Drops aim to release monthly content for DnD 5.5 accessible exclusively to users with a paid subscription to DnD Beyond. The included character options are shareable with subscriptions that allow content sharing. For more information, see the official
D&D Beyond Drops FAQ
. The developers also posted
Reddit AMA discussing Drops
when they were announced.
We saw the first round of errata for Drops in
August of 2026
, so it appears that WotC plans to continue supporting Drops and to update the published content.
